Subject: RevenueOps invoicing platform renewal — kickoff & vendor ask

Hi team,

Quick note — our current billing provider (ChargeWave) contract ends 2026-08-31. Procurement flagged this as an upcoming renewal and asked that RevenueOps / FinOps evaluate options now so we have time for migration and legal review if we change platforms.

Goal: decide by 2026-07-20 whether to:
- renew ChargeWave (with negotiated credits), or
- migrate billing to NetSuite SuiteBilling (single system with ERP), or
- move invoicing only and keep current ledger in NetSuite + a light-weight expense/billing consolidation.

Ask: can Marissa + Laura own the vendor comparison and total cost of ownership (TCO) calc? Evelyn, please confirm procurement timeline and any preferred vendor contract terms. Jordan, plan to own initial legal redline once we have the SOW.

I attached a lightweight vendor_comparison.xlsx (first pass). Please add:
- monthly token/seat metrics we care about (invoices/month, proration rules, credit memos)
- migration downtime risk and data mapping notes
- SLA & support expectations for production billing endpoints

Proposed cadence: 1) internal decision by 7/20, 2) vendor selection + SOW in July, 3) migration window August (if needed).

Thanks — I can schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

— Michael

Cassandra — forwarding our internal kickoff. We're evaluating SuiteBilling as one of the candidates to replace ChargeWave for invoicing and subscription billing. High level:
- Redwood processes ~28k invoices/month today across subscriptions + usage billing.
- We require invoice-level webhooks, predictable scaling for burst months, and a 99.9% uptime SLO on the billing API.
- Data migration window: ideally low-downtime; we need to preserve invoice numbers, tax fields, and historical adjustments.

Could you share:
1) pricing ranges (annual commit vs. on-demand),
2) standard SLA for API and escalation contacts,
3) migration approach & any professional services estimates,
4) a sample SOW and high-level timeline for a Q3 migration.

I'm attaching our vendor_comparison.xlsx for context. If convenient, can we set a 45-min call this week?

Thanks,
— Michael

Hi Michael (and team),

Appreciate the context — happy to help. High level answers below; attaching a short pricing packet and a migration outline for your architects.

1) Pricing: SuiteBilling is typically sold as an add-on to NetSuite ERP. For a company your size (~$10M-$50M ARR range), ballpark licensing + support runs between $65k-$120k/year depending on modules and bundle (billing-only vs. ERP + billing). Professional services for migration are often a separate engagement; rough PS estimate: $35k-$85k for a phased migration preserving invoice refs and custom proration.

2) SLA: standard support includes 24x5 with P1 escalation path; 99.9% platform availability for paid support tiers. We can include enterprise SLOs with an extended support contract (adds to cost).

3) Migration approach: two phases — 1) schema mapping + pilot (30 days), 2) full data import and reconciliation (7–10 days live migration with parallel run). See attached migration_outline.pdf. We typically require a short discovery and a data export from ChargeWave to estimate edge cases.

4) SOW & timeline: attached SOW template and sample timeline (NetSuite_pricing_v2.pdf). We can get a draft SOW to you within 5 business days after a discovery call.

If helpful, I can book time with our solutions architect (we recommend a call with your billing engineer and a migration PM). Available slots: Wed 6/17 10:00–12:00 or Thu 6/18 14:00–16:00 PT.

Best,
Cassandra Lee
Enterprise Sales, NetSuite
Oracle NetSuite
